findings.title: AuthorizationGrant.audience_pubkey is NOT in binding_message — full grant-access-theft via field substitution (L3 sibling cross-confirmation)
findings.site: crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:267 (field decl) + crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:390-425 (binding_message construction omits audience_pubkey) + crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:442-460 (ARM 2 trusts audience_pubkey as authoritative)
findings.reproducer: 1) Take any legitimate signed AuthorizationGrant where audience_binding = blake3(alice_pubkey) and audience_pubkey = Some(alice_pubkey). 2) Substitute ONLY the audience_pubkey field with attacker_pubkey (leave audience_binding, ucan, scope, key_material, issuer_verifying_key, binding_sig all intact). 3) Call grant.verify_binding(audience_binding) → SUCCEEDS (audience_pubkey is not in the binding-message at line 418-423). 4) Attacker presents grant via UcanBlobsHandler.validate_request_for_connection with connection_endpoint_id = attacker_pubkey. ARM 2 at line 455 compares connection_endpoint_id to grant.audience_pubkey (= attacker_pubkey) → PASSES. ARM 5 verify_binding → PASSES. ARMs 3,4,6 unaffected. Attacker now uses Alice's grant as themselves. Grep reproducer: `grep -A30 'fn binding_message' crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs` shows binding takes (ucan, key_material, audience, scope) — no audience_pubkey arg. Verifier confirmation: `grep -A40 'fn verify_binding' crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs` shows it re-constructs the message with same 4 args.
findings.code_quote_binding_omission: fn binding_message(ucan: &UcanEnvelope, key_material: &GrantKeyMaterial, audience: &Cid, scope: Option<&crate::restricted_spec::RestrictedScope>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, _> { ... msg.extend_from_slice(audience.as_bytes()); msg.extend_from_slice(&scope_len.to_le_bytes()); msg.extend_from_slice(&scope_bytes); ... }  // NO audience_pubkey or issuer_verifying_key segment
findings.missing_runtime_check: grep -rn 'audience_pubkey.*audience_binding\|derive_cid_from_pubkey' crates/ → ZERO hits. The structural coupling (audience_binding = blake3(audience_pubkey) at issue-time per authorization_grant.rs:515-516) is NOT re-derived at verify-time. The wave-3e production wire-up doc (line 511-514) explicitly says 'production wire-up will route through the proper did:key CID derivation when grants flow from the real DID-registration surface' — this is the unimplemented part that makes the attack work at v1-beta.
findings.threat_model: Same-attack-class as L3-r1-1 closed for `scope` field (post-sign scope-widening). Identical shape: a security-bearing field in AuthorizationGrant is NOT folded into binding_message; downstream consumer trusts the field as if signed; attacker substitutes the field post-sign. L3-r1-1 closed scope; this BLOCKER says audience_pubkey is the same attack on a DIFFERENT field in the same struct. The fix did not sweep siblings (per feedback_d17_same_file_sweep_recurrence).
findings.fix_now_shape: Extend binding_message signature: `fn binding_message(ucan, key_material, audience: &Cid, scope: Option<_>, audience_pubkey: Option<&[u8]>, issuer_verifying_key: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, _>`. Encode audience_pubkey as `audience_pubkey_len_u32_le || audience_pubkey_bytes` (same length-prefix shape as scope; None encodes as 0_u32_le for back-compat with wave-3b fixtures). Encode issuer_verifying_key as fixed 32-byte segment (Ed25519 is fixed-width; no length prefix needed). Bump BINDING_SIG_DOMAIN v2→v3 (same shape as L3-r1-1 bumped v1→v2). Update verify_binding to thread `self.audience_pubkey.as_deref()` + `&self.issuer_verifying_key`. Update all 4 test-constructor sites (issue_for_test + issue_with_nbf_for_test + 2 distinct ones) to pass the new args. Estimated LOC: ~80 + 2-3 attack-class regression pins. Cross-language mirror per §3.5g: not applicable (this is internal-to-Rust cap-policy; no TS wire surface). Wire-format inventory update: BINDING_SIG_DOMAIN tag bump v2→v3 + binding-message-layout v2→v3 → both ADD to V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md.

findings.title: AuthorizationGrant.issuer_verifying_key is NOT in binding_message — same-attack-class sibling of BLOCKER-1; allows issuer-attribution forgery + revocation-bypass
findings.site: crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:257 (field decl) + crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:653-695 (verify_binding accepts the carried key as authoritative for its own verification) + crates/benten-drop/src/envelope_sig.rs:92 (same shape at DropBundle layer — issuer_verifying_key explicitly zeroed in signed payload)
findings.reproducer: 1) Take any legitimate AuthorizationGrant where issuer_verifying_key = legit_issuer_pubkey + binding_sig = legit_issuer_sig. 2) Attacker generates their own Ed25519 keypair (attacker_kp). 3) Attacker re-computes binding_sig as attacker_kp.sign(binding_message(ucan, key_material, audience_binding, scope)) — the SAME binding_message because no fields they changed are in it. 4) Substitute (issuer_verifying_key=attacker_kp.public_key().to_bytes(), binding_sig=new_sig). 5) verify_binding(audience_binding) → SUCCEEDS (attacker's sig verifies against attacker's pubkey). 6) Downstream consumer that says 'this grant was issued by grant.issuer_verifying_key' now attributes Alice's legitimate grant to attacker. Revocation lists keyed on issuer_verifying_key are bypassed (attacker substitutes issuer-key to dodge a revocation entry against the legit issuer's key). Grep reproducer: `grep -A40 'fn verify_binding' crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs` shows verify_binding takes vk from self.issuer_verifying_key — same as caller asking 'is this signature valid for the key the message ITSELF says signed it?'.
findings.threat_model: This is the classic 'attacker controls the asserted signer identity' vulnerability — verify_binding's positive answer means only 'someone with the private key matching the carried public key signed these bytes', not 'the legitimate issuer signed these bytes'. The legitimate-issuer claim depends on a TRUST chain from issuer_verifying_key to a registered DID-root, which does NOT exist as a runtime check at v1-beta (the only such check is the upstream UCAN chain validation, which is bypassed if the grant is consumed direct without a UCAN-chain walk against an external trust anchor). Damage scenarios: (a) revocation-bypass — revoke 'all grants signed by alice_pubkey'; attacker re-attributes the grant to 'bob_pubkey' to dodge. (b) audit-trail-forgery — incident response can't trust grant.issuer_verifying_key as ground truth. (c) cross-trust-zone re-attribution if any zone keys grants to issuer_verifying_key (e.g., a zone that says 'admit grants whose issuer is in this allowlist' is bypassed by substituting issuer to a permitted one).
findings.fix_now_shape: Include issuer_verifying_key in binding_message per BLOCKER-1's shape (fixed 32-byte segment between scope and end). Also extend crates/benten-drop/src/envelope_sig.rs::build_envelope_message to INCLUDE issuer_verifying_key in the signed payload (currently line 92 explicitly zeroes it; this is the same anti-pattern). Same-attack-class sweep per feedback_d17_same_file_sweep_recurrence: audit ALL fields excluded from signed payloads across the workspace — `grep -rn 'for_sig\..*= Vec::new\|for_sig\..*= 0' crates/` finds the systematic anti-pattern. Bundle into BLOCKER-1's binding_message v3 bump.
